Ubhayavedānta
(‘Vedānta [that accepts] both’)
------------------------------------------
Vedānta has branched off into three main streams: Advaita, Viśiṣṭādvaita and द्वैत.
Unlike the Advaita and the द्वैत philosophies which accept only the प्रस्थानत्रय (See PRASTHĀNATRAYA.) as authoritative, the Viśiṣṭādvaita of Rāmānuja (A. D. 1017-1137) accords equal status to the Sanskrit प्रस्थानत्रय as also to the Divyaprabandham (Tamil works of the आऌवार्स्). Hence it is called उभयवेदान्त, Vedānta that accepts both (= ubhaya) the authorities.

Ubhayabhāratī
------------------------------------------
The traditional biographies of शङ्कर (A. D. 788-820) like the Śaṅkara-digvijaya of Mādhava-विद्यारण्य (14th century A. D.) state that after शङ्कर vanquished Maṇḍana Miśra—a great scholar of Mīmāṁsā philosophy—his wife भारती challenged him for an intellectual debate. She was finally humbled by शङ्कर and like her husband, she too decided to become a recluse and a disciple. She is said to have followed शङ्कर up to Śṛṅgerī and settled down there.
She has been described as an इन्चर्नतिओन् of सरस्वती, born on earth due to a curse of the sage दुर्वासस्.
The temple of Śāradāmbā at Śṛṅgerī is her temple.
Since she acted as a judge in the debate between शङ्कर and Maṇḍana—for both of them—she came to be known as उभयभारती (ubhaya = both).
Her original name has also been mentioned as Sarasavāṇī, Vāṇī and अम्बा.
